Frequently asked questions:
Why 10Gbps speed not achieved?
1.Please contact the manufacturer of the motherboard and check the following information.
1). PCI-E slot protocol requires PCIe version 3.0 or higher.
2). The lanes assigned to the PCI-E interface are x4 or higher (The lanes assigned to the PCI-E interface are x4 or higher. (x1,x2 channels are also available, but the speed will not be reached).

2.When using a USB pcie card, USB devices have performance limitations on the throughput/performance of the card's data transfer. This depends on the USB protocol and cable material of the end device.you can check if your external USB device supports 10Gbps bandwidth by consulting your external USB device vendor.
Why is this USB 3.2 port detected as USB 3.1 by the computer system?
According to the latest USB-IF standard: the USB-A ports on this card is USB 3.2 Gen 2x1 = USB 3.1 Gen 2 = USB 10Gbps.

description: The Instek SPD-3606 triple-output switching DC power supply unit provides a constant source of DC voltage and current for powering and testing electronic devices. The power supply unit (PSU) has two dual-range outputs that each provide DC voltage from 0 to 30V and current from 0 to 6 amp, or DC voltage from 0 to 60V and current from 0 to 3 amp, with adjustable output. A third output supplies an adjustable voltage between 0.1V and 5VDC and a fixed current of 3 amp. The PSU's high power-conversion efficiency reduces the unit's energy consumption. The PSU simultaneously shows voltage and current readings for each output. The 0 to 30V outputs can be connected in series to supply more voltage, or they can be connected in parallel to supply more current. When in tracking mode, one output can be set to supply a percentage of the voltage of the second output. A built-in cooling fan with three speeds helps prevent overheating. Reverse polarity, overvoltage protection, and an output on/off switch help prevent damage to the PSU and the device under test, and the unit automatically selects between 115V and 230V line voltage.
H is the vertical distance from lowest to highest point, W is the horizontal distance from left to right, and D is the horizontal distance from front to back.

Power supply units (also known as PSUs, AC power supplies, DC power supplies, and battery eliminators) provide AC or DC voltage to power or test devices such as tools, appliances, and electronic components. The PSU draws energy from a line source such as a wall socket and converts it to a constant, specified amount of voltage or current that is then outputted to a connected device. In general, a power supply unit will be classified as either a linear PSU (also known as a linear regulation or line-frequency PSU) or a switched PSU (also known as a switching-mode power supply, SMPS, or switcher). Typically, a linear PSU has a simpler design and provides a faster transient response time and less electrical interference and noise than a switched PSU. A switched PSU is often smaller, lighter, and more efficient than a linear PSU and generates less heat. The transient response time of a PSU indicates how quickly the PSU can resume the desired constant output after a sudden change in input. Ripple voltage or current indicates how much unfiltered noise and AC voltage or current is present at the output of a filtered power supply operated at full load. The temperature coefficient is the percent average change in output voltage per degree centigrade of change in ambient temperature. Fuses, current limiters, and other forms of overload protection can be built into the PSU to help protect against voltage spikes or short-circuiting.

GW Instek manufactures test and measurement equipment such as oscilloscopes, spectrum analyzers, signal testers, and video surveillance systems. The company, founded in 1975 and headquartered in Taipei, Taiwan, meets International Organization for Standardization (ISO) standards 9002 and 14001.

Additional Ports for Workspace Flexibility The enclosure features a DisplayPort output port, enabling you to connect a DisplayPort monitor to your computer through the Thunderbolt 3 enclosure, with resolutions up to 4K 60Hz. Product Warning
1. Compatibility Check First
This cable is only compatible with 12PIN modular power supplies (matching the 12PIN port specification). Do NOT use with non-12PIN PSUs or incompatible brands/models—incorrect use may damage your PSU, GPU, or other PC components.
2. Power Load Limitation
Supports a maximum total power output of 300W (via dual 8Pin connectors). Do NOT connect to high-power GPUs exceeding this limit (e.g., some overclocked RTX 5090 models) without confirming your PSU’s power capacity.
3. Secure Connection Required
Ensure all connectors (12PIN to PSU, 8Pin to GPU) are fully inserted and locked in place before powering on your PC. Loose connections may cause short circuits, power outages, or hardware damage.
4. No Disassembly/Modification
Do NOT cut, splice, or modify the cable’s wires or connectors. Tampering will void any product warranty and create serious safety hazards (e.g., electric shock, fire risk).
5. Static Electricity Protection
Handle the cable with anti-static precautions (e.g., anti-static wristband) during installation to avoid damaging sensitive GPU/PSU electronics.
6. Check Cable Condition
Inspect the cable for frayed wires, cracked connectors, or damage before use. Discontinue use immediately if any defects are found and contact customer support.
7. Professional Installation Recommended
If you are unfamiliar with PC power supply wiring, ask a qualified technician to install the cable to avoid incorrect connections.

Tip 2: If there's no display (fans spin but keyboard lights remain unresponsive when pressing Caps Lock), verify the motherboard and CPU power connections, ensure memory modules are properly seated, and confirm CPU/memory model compatibility and condition; if issues persist after these checks, clear CMOS

All easily accessible with tool-less top and side panels alongside floating storage sleds that eject from the rear of the case for intuitive drive maintenance.

Colour: Black (terminal housing)

Important Notes:
1. Voltage and Power Compatibility
Suitable only for standard 12V/5V PC power supplies (default output voltage for XH2.54 mini 4-pin connectors). Connecting to industrial-grade high-voltage power sources is strictly prohibited to prevent device damage.
Maximum supported power per cable ≤100W. Connecting multiple 3.5-inch HDDs is not recommended (each 3.5-inch HDD consumes approximately 10-15W; connect 1-2 drives per cable) to prevent overloading and overheating.
2. Installation Guidelines
Before installation, ensure the PC power supply is switched off and the power cable is disconnected to prevent live connections causing short circuits to the motherboard, hard drive, or power connectors.
When inserting connectors, align them with the latch direction (SATA connectors feature a foolproof design). Avoid forceful insertion or removal to prevent damage to connector pins.
When organising chassis cables, avoid excessive bending (minimum bend radius ≥2cm) and keep them clear of rotating components such as CPU fans and graphics card fans to prevent entanglement or abrasion.
3. Compatibility Verification
Confirm your power supply features an XH2.54 standard small 4-pin connector (distinct from the larger 4-pin variant) to prevent incompatibility issues.
Compatible only with SATA interface devices (2.5-inch SSDs, 3.5-inch HDDs, SATA optical drives). Not compatible with M.2 interfaces, NVMe protocol devices, or IDE interface devices.
4. Routine Use and Maintenance
During prolonged use, periodically inspect cables for damage: cease use immediately and replace if insulation is compromised or connectors show oxidation (rust/darkening) to prevent short-circuit risks.
Keep cables away from high-temperature components (e.g., CPU coolers, graphics cards) and ensure adequate case ventilation to prevent accelerated cable ageing.
5. After-Sales and Warranty Information
If a connected device fails to respond, first verify that the interface is securely seated and that power is being supplied correctly. Alternatively, test compatibility by connecting another SATA device.
This product warranty covers the cables themselves only. We accept no liability for damage resulting from improper installation, abnormal voltage, or inherent device faults.

title: GLOTRENDS UEX103 600mm PCIe 3.0 X1 to X4 Riser Cable (PCIe 3.0 X1 Bandwidth) for PCIe WiFi Card, M.2 PCIe Card, Firewire Card, USB PCIe Card, Sound Card, etc
features: If your motherboard's PCIe X1 slot is covered by the GPU next to it, this product can extend this PCIe X1 slot out 600mm farther, and convert it to a PCIe X4 slot.
With the low profile design on the male side, only 6mm high space (Motherboard to the bottom edge of GPU) is needed for installation. No problem in most cases.
Work with PCIe X1/X4 cards, such as PCIe Wifi Card, M.2 PCIe Card, Firewire Card, USB PCIe Card, Sound Card, etc.
Maximum speed is PCIe 3.0 X1 (~1GB/s). If your slot is PCIe 2.0 X16, it can only reach the speed of PCIe 2.0 X1 (~0.5GB/s).

Another advantage: the 600mm round wire can be twisted at any angle, so the position of the female side is virtually unlimited. In addition, the bottom surface is insulating foam, which can be labeled with self-adhesive tape (Not included) so that the female side can be mounted at any angle.

Plug and Play, and compatible with Windows/Mac OS/Linux/NAS. If the PC crashes or has blue screens after installation. Please re-insert the PCIe X4 riser cable and make sure all devices are properly secured.
Operating Voltage: 12 Voltage; Output Power: 30W at max
